newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Crowds seek first glimpse of Kabila at inauguration.
newsitem.headline: Crowds seek first glimpse of Kabila at inauguration.

text.p: Thousands of Kinshasa residents turned out on Thursday to catch their first real-life glimpse of self-proclaimed president Laurent Kabila at his inauguration as head of state at the capital's main sports stadium.
Airport sources said that Uganda's President Yoweri Museveni and Burundi's Pierre Buyoya had arrived to attend the ceremony, due to start around noon (1100 GMT).
Kabila, whose forces drove veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko from power in a seven-month civil war, has kept out of the public eye since arriving in Kinshasa on May 20.
Thousands of people gathered in the Martyrs Stadium where Mobutu's former military band serenaded them.

"We automatically have unconditional respect for the head of state," Major Kawamonoko Ngodia, commander of the 250-strong brass band, told Reuters. "It does not matter who it is. Before it was Mobutu, now it is President Kabila."

The government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, former Zaire, declared Thursday a public holiday in the capital and state radio broadcast repeated messages urging the population to turn out in force for the inauguration.
"Today is an historic day for our country," the radio said. "All Kinois (Kinshasa citizens) are requested to turn out at the stadium for the investiture," it added.
The Chinese-built stadium, formerly named Kamanyola after Mobutu's most famous battle against an early revolt, holds up to 100,000 people.

Kabila's whose forces marched into Kinshasa on May 17, on Wednesday decreed himself sweeping powers to run the country until the adoption of a new transitional constitution by a promised constituent council.
Earlier, his soldiers broke up a third opposition protest in under a week.
Wednesday's 15-article decree, broadcast on state radio and television, said individual liberties would be guaranteed subject to respect of the law, public order and morals.
"The government conducts the policies of the nation as defined by the president," the decree added.

Mobutu ruled mineral-rich Zaire for over three decades, during which rampant corruption drained what is potentially one of Africa's richest nations. Foreign and domestic pressure forced him to abandon his near absolute powers in 1990 for a democratic transition but implementation dragged.
Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo has banned political activity and public demonstrations, citing the need to preserve public order.
